gallery.title: File:Jacqueline Bouvier Kennedy Onassis Hall.jpg
gallery.description: Jacqueline Bouvier Kennedy Onassis Hall is located at 2222 I Street NW in the Foggy Bottom neighborhood of Washington, D.C. It is a residence hall for George Washington University students. The building was originally known as Milton Hall. It was constructed in 1938 and designed by Robert O. Scholz. The building is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and District of Columbia Inventory of Historic Sites.

gallery.filename: 605-609 21st Street NW and 2031 F Street NW.jpg
gallery.title: File:605-609 21st Street NW and 2031 F Street NW.jpg
gallery.source: 605-609 21st Street NW and 2031 F Street NW
gallery.description: The former houses located at 605-609 21st Street NW and 2031 F Street NW in the Foggy Bottom neighborhood of Washington, D.C., were built in 1897 and designed by Arthur B. Heaton. The buildings are contributing properties to the George Washington University-Old West End Historic District. The building on the left is offices for The GW Hatchet.

gallery.title: File:Lenthall Houses GWU.jpg
gallery.description: The Lenthall Houses (also known as the John Lenthall Houses) are located at 606 and 610 21st Street NW in the Foggy Bottom neighborhood of Washington, D.C. The Federal-style homes were built in 1800 by John Lenthall, principal assistant to Benjamin Latrobe during construction of the United States Capitol. They were originally located at 614 and 616 19th Street NW, but were moved in 1978 to prevent demolition (the old location is now occupied by one of the World Bank buildings). The Lenthall Houses are now owned by George Washington University and are listed on the National Register of Historic Places and District of Columbia Inventory of Historic Sites. They are also contributing properties to the George Washington University-Old West End Historic District.

gallery.title: File:F Street House - Washington, D.C.jpg
gallery.description: The Steedman-Ray House, now known as the F Street House, is located at 1925 F Street NW in the Foggy Bottom neighborhood of Washington, D.C. It serves as the residence of George Washington University's president. The house was constructed in 1849 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and the District of Columbia Inventory of Historic Sites. It is also a contributing property to the George Washington University-Old West End Historic District.

gallery.title: File:Thurston Hall.jpg
gallery.description: Mabel Nelson Thurston Hall, also known as Thurston Hall, is a residence hall for George Washington University students located at 1900 F Street NW in Washington, D.C. It was constructed in 1928 as the Park Central Apartments and designed by Harvey H. Warwick. It is a contributing property to the George Washington University/Old West End Historic District.

gallery.filename: Union Methodist Episcopal Church - Building XX.jpg
gallery.title: File:Union Methodist Episcopal Church - Building XX.jpg
gallery.source: Union Methodist Episcopal Church - Building XX
gallery.description: Union Methodist Episcopal Church, now known as Building XX, is located at 814 20th Street NW in Washington, D.C. It was constructed in 1848 and expanded in 1910. During the Civil War the church served as a hospital for Union soldiers. It is a contributing property to the George Washington University/Old West End Historic District. The building served as a place of worship until 1975 and currently houses office space for George Washington University's Columbian College of Arts and Sciences.

gallery.title: File:1917 and 1919 I Street NW.jpg
gallery.description: The building located at 1917 I Street NW (right) in Washington, D.C., constructed in 1892 as a private residence for Dr. James T. Sothoron, was designed by architect Paul J. Pelz. It was later the residence of William D. Hassett, a journalist and author who served as Secretary to the President for Franklin D. Roosevelt and Harry S. Truman, and office space for the National Federation of Business and Professional Women's Clubs. The building located at 1919 I Street NW was constructed in 1960.
